{{Short description|German statistician}}
'''Matthias Schonlau''' (born 9 November 1967)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2001015222.html|title=Schonlau, Matthias, 1967-|publisher=Library of Congress Name Authority File|accessdate=4 January 2019}}</ref> is a German Professor of [[statistics]] and [[actuarial science]] at the [[University of Waterloo]].

==Early life and career==
Matthias Schonlau was born in [[Höxter]], Germany. He attended [[University of Ulm]] for an undergrad degree but never obtained it because he became enrolled into a master's program at the [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]]<ref name=niss1>{{cite news|publisher=NISS|url=https://www.niss.org/news/former-postdoc-profile-matthias-schonlau|title=Former Postdoc Profile - Matthias Schonlau|accessdate=4 January 2019}}</ref> from which he graduated in 1993.<ref name=uwaterloo/> In 1997 Matthias got his Ph.D. from the [[University of Waterloo]].<ref name=uwaterloo>{{cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/statistics-and-actuarial-science/people-profiles/matthias-schonlau|title=Matthias Schonlau|date=19 February 2015 |accessdate=4 January 2019}}</ref>

From 1997 to 1999 he was a researcher for the [[National Institute of Statistical Sciences]] under mentorship of Alan Karr and during the same time worked as a [[security hacker]] at the [[AT&T Labs]].<ref name=niss1/>

From 1999 to 2011 he worked as [[Survey methodology|survey methodologist]] for [[RAND Corporation]] under mentorship of Sally Morton<ref name=niss1/> at its [[Santa Monica]] headquarters and eventually moved to their Pittsburgh office.<ref name=niss2>{{cite news|url=https://www.niss.org/news/schonlau-receives-niss-2018-distinguished-alumni-award|title=Schonlau Receives NISS 2018 Distinguished Alumni Award|author=Glenn Johnson|publisher=NISS|date=8 August 2018|accessdate=4 January 2019}}</ref> From 2009 to 2010 he attended a sabbatical at the [[German Institute for Economic Research]] which was hosted in cooperation with the [[Max Planck Institute for Human Development]]<ref name=uwaterloo/> and from 2015 to 2016 he was a [[visiting scholar]] at the [[University of Auckland]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.stats.org.nz/app/uploads/2017/09/newsletter76.pdf|title=Statistics at University of Auckland|author=Karen Lee|journal=Newsletter|publisher=University of Auckland|number=76|year=2016|page=16|issn=0112-2649|oclc=247483856}}</ref> From 2015 to 2018 he was a member of the [[European Survey Research Association]] and in the end of 2018 became the president of the survey methods section of the [[Statistical Society of Canada]]. He is also an associate editor of the ''[[Survey Research Methods]]''.<ref name=niss2/>

==Recognition==
Schonlau is an ''NISS Distinguished Alumni Award'' recipient.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://ssc.ca/en/publications/ssc-liaison/vol-32-5-october-2018/national-institute-statistical-sciences-niss-award|title=The National Institute of Statistical Sciences (NISS) Award Granted|publisher=NISS|date=October 2018|volume=32|issue=5}}</ref> He was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|title=ASA Fellows list|publisher=American Statistical Association|accessdate=2020-06-01}}</ref> In 2022 he was the recipient of a Humboldt Prize.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrviewhumboldtians%5BpPersonId%5D=1223423|title=Prof. Dr. Matthias Schonlau|publisher=Humboldt Foundation|accessdate=2023-11-19}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Matthias Schonlau is married to Dr. Karla Kaphengst, a physician from the University Health and Counselling Centre. They have two children.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/en/about/news-and-events-5/news/news-2016/2016/02/digging-deeper-in-the-text-mine.html|title=Digging deeper in the text mine|publisher=University of Auckland|date=9 February 2016|accessdate=4 January 2019}}</ref>
